memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Adam named his wife Eve, because she would become the mother of all the living. — Gen 3:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Isn't the timing of this verse remarkable? God has just spoken of thorns, sweat, and returning to the dust. The word "death" still hangs in the air. And in that very moment, Adam turns to his wife and gives her a name that means life: Eve, "the mother of all the living."

This is more than a tender gesture. It is a quiet act of faith. Adam has just heard that he will return to dust — yet he names his wife for life, not death. Somewhere in his heart, he has taken hold of God's promise. God had said the offspring of the woman would one day crush the serpent (Gen 3:15). So Adam looks past the sentence of death and believes there is a future, that life will go on, that God's word of hope is true.

What a beautiful picture of faith. Faith is not the denial of hard realities; Adam does not pretend the curse away. Faith is choosing to believe God's promise in the middle of hard realities — naming life even while standing in the shadow of death.

Dear friend, you may be facing your own season of thorns and dust today. Faith does not ask you to ignore it. But like Adam, you can look past the difficulty to the promise of God, and dare to speak the language of hope. For the God who promised life in Eden has given us life in fullness through Christ, who conquered death itself (Jn 11:25).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you need to speak the language of hope in the middle of a hard season?
2. What promise of God can you take hold of even while facing difficulty?
3. How does Christ's victory over death fill your view of the future with hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that even under the shadow of death, You give reasons for hope. Like Adam, help me to take hold of Your promises and speak faith into my hard seasons. Thank You that in Jesus You have given me life that death can never take away. Amen.
